The petitioner through instant petition under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India is
seeking direction to respondent No. 1 to re-issue his passport.
2.  The petitioner was issued passport which was valid upto 26.12.2014.
Three FIRs have been registered against the petitioner.

FIR No.98 dated 06.06.2014, under Sections 420,120-B of IPC,
registered at Police Station, City Kharar, District SAS Nagar Mohali, stands quashed.
In FIR No.62 dated 22.03.2014, under Sections 120-B, 420, 406, 465, 467, 468, 471 of IPC, registered against the petitioner at Police Station, Phase-I, Mohali, the petitioner stands acquitted.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that case of the petitioner is squarely covered by judgment of this Court in Mohan Lal @ Mohna vs. Union of India and others 2023 SCC Online P&H 1391.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for Union of India, who on advance notice is present in Court, submits that petitioner filed application in 2018 which has already been closed.
The petitioner is at liberty to file a fresh application which shall be processed in accordance with law.
5. Faced with this, learned counsel for the petitioner seeks permission to withdraw with liberty to approach passport authority.
6. In the wake of statements of both sides, the petition stands disposed of.
